title: Film Study: The New-Look Blazers Are a Blast
contentHtml:
Amid an avalanche of gut-punch injuries to star players—the latest being Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring flare-up—it’s important to revel in fun basketball when it presents itself.

(It’s also important for the league to have a deeper conversation about what is going on with player health. We’ve reached a point where explaining this away as a combination of randomness and teams being more cautious with any hamstring or calf strain is insufficient. It doesn’t pass the smell test. The league investigates all of this and consults with its teams’ sports-science pros, but it needs to shoot player health and availability up the priority scale—and share whatever findings it has with fans. It’s no longer enough for Adam Silver to say “We’re open to everything” and “82 games isn’t set in stone” every six months at scripted press conferences.)

Subscribe now

To wit: The undefeated Memphis Grizzlies will face the undefeated Portland Trail Blazers on Thursday in a meeting of two of the league’s happiest early-season stories—a game that doubles as the Ja Morant Bowl. Reality will come for both soon as schedules toughen and shooting luck normalizes, but both teams have shown enough to at least nudge up whatever prior expectations you had for them. With the Denver Nuggets scuffling early and Anthony Edwards out for up to two months, the top six in the West appears more permeable than it did two weeks ago. Both these teams might have something to say.

I was high-ish on the Grizzlies coming into this season, though not this high, and Ty Jerome is hopping on The Zach Lowe Show Thursday, so we can leave them aside here. The Blazers confused me, even though I defended their no-risk, unknown-reward grab for Morant—an out-of-nowhere gamble that introduced obvious questions about spacing, perimeter defense, and the glut of ball handlers suddenly orbiting incumbent All-Star and driving machine Deni Avdija.

The new-look Blazers leapfrogged the Los Angeles Lakers for the no. 1 spot in offensive efficiency after beating L.A. on the road Tuesday behind 89 combined points from Damian Lillard, Jrue Holiday, Avdija, and Morant—and four more triples from the scorching Toumani Camara. (How good does his contract look?)
